title: Tricky UL Endings
kidRule: The 'ul' sound at the end of a word is usually spelled L-E, like in EXAMPLE. Sometimes it is E-L (often after M, N, or V, like in TUNNEL) or A-L, and those words just have to be remembered.
hint: Listen to the 'ul' sound at the end. That little sound can be spelled in more than one way. Which way looks right in this word?
reminder: The 'ul' ending has three spellings: L-E, E-L, and A-L. If your first try did not work, try another one!

check.question: Why does EXAMPLE end with L-E?
check.correctAnswer: Because L-E is the most common way to spell the 'ul' sound at the end of a word!
distractors: Because the E at the end makes the A say its name
Because words about school always end with L-E

words.def: A long hole under the ground or through a mountain that you can go through.
words.sent: The train zoomed through a dark tunnel.
words.story: The Channel Tunnel lets trains zoom under the sea between England and France!
words.card: The *tun*a fish sang all the way through the *tunnel*!

words.def: One thing that shows what the others in a group are like.
words.sent: A robin is an example of a bird.
words.story: A dictionary often gives an example sentence for a word, to show you how the word is used!
words.card: For *example*, never plug your guitar *amp* into a pineapple!

words.def: A thick, warm forest full of tall trees, vines, and wild animals.
words.sent: Monkeys swing through the trees in the jungle.
words.story: Scientists think more than half of all the kinds of plants and animals on Earth live in rainforest jungles!
words.card: In *Jun*e, the monkeys threw a *jungle* party with banana cake!

words.def: One of the soft, colorful parts of a flower.
words.sent: A pink petal floated down from the tree.
words.story: Bright petals work like signs that show bees and butterflies where the sweet nectar is!
words.card: My *pet* snail wears a rose *petal* as a fancy hat!

words.def: A big round container with curved sides, often made of wood.
words.sent: Rain filled the barrel beside the barn.
words.story: A person who makes wooden barrels is called a cooper!
words.card: The monkey hid a candy *bar* at the bottom of the *barrel*!

words.def: Something wonderful and surprising that seems almost impossible.
words.sent: It was a miracle that the tiny kitten found its way home.
words.story: In 1980 the United States hockey team beat the mighty Soviet team at the Olympics, and the game is still called the 'Miracle on Ice'!
words.card: Look in the *mir*ror: it is a *miracle*, my hair is combed!

words.def: To go from one place to another, often far away.
words.sent: We travel to the lake by train every summer.
words.story: Arctic terns travel farther than any other animal, flying from the top of the world to the bottom and back every year!
words.card: *Tra*-la-la, I *travel* to the moon on a flying sofa!

words.def: A big building where doctors and nurses take care of people who are sick or hurt.
words.sent: The baby was born in a hospital near our house.
words.story: The word is a cousin of 'hotel' and 'host', because they all come from an old Latin word for a guest!
words.card: The llama promised not to *spit* inside the *hospital*!

words.def: A special time when lots of people get together to celebrate with music, food, or games.
words.sent: We ate noodles at the lantern festival.
words.story: At a festival in Spain called La Tomatina, thousands of people throw squishy tomatoes at each other just for fun!
words.card: The frog *fest* was the hoppiest *festival* in the whole swamp!

words.def: A thing you ride that has two wheels, pedals, and handlebars.
words.sent: She rode her bicycle to the park.
words.story: The very first bicycles had no pedals at all: riders pushed along the ground with their feet!
words.card: The bear rode a *bicycle* down the *icy* hill and did not stop until spring!
